study type: Cross-sectional observational study (human samples) and in vitro experimental study (trophoblasts)
exposure: Vitamin D levels (maternal and cord blood plasma 25(OH)D(3))
outcome: Placental efficiency (fetal to placental weight ratio)
cohort: Normal-weight (BMI<25) and obese (BMI>30) women with uncomplicated pregnancies at term, from whom maternal and cord blood plasma and placental samples were collected upon C-section.
finding: Vitamin D deficiency is at least partially responsible for mitochondrial dysfunction and increased inflammation in the placentae of obese women, with calcitriol treatment improving mitochondrial respiration and reversing IL-18 expression in isolated trophoblasts.
